edits.name: Half page for Jordan: how to tell that Happy is down
edits.description: Jordan gets a printed half page that tells her how to recognise that Happy is down, that nothing is broken, and who to call. After a power cut Happy stays down until Tony unlocks the Mac at home, as the roadmap row he chose says. A sealed envelope with one password, so that she could bring Happy back herself, is added only if Tony says yes (waits on Q12) and his own unlock test passes.
edits.example: A power cut while Tony is out. Happy stops answering, and Jordan reads the half page: no reply within a few minutes means Happy is down, nothing in the house is broken, and it comes back when Tony unlocks the Mac.
edits.how: No new software. Tony writes and prints a half page for Jordan: (1) how to tell that Happy is down: no reply within a few minutes, or the error line a parent sees when a turn fails, worded from what test T8 showed; (2) nothing is broken: after a power cut the Mac waits at the disk-unlock screen and Happy stays down until Tony unlocks it; (3) who to call. No envelope, no Terminal commands and no alert to her phone in this form. Only if Tony says yes under Q12: he first runs T10 alone (list the users enabled for disk unlock, then one plain restart, not the planned-reboot command) to see whether the happy user's password alone brings Happy back to answering texts. If it passes, one sealed envelope holds only that password and the page gains one step: type it at the Mac. The house scripts stay Tony-only.
depends_on: T8 (wave A, first phase): Tony has seen on his own phone what a failed turn looks like, so the page is worded from that
waits on Q12 for everything beyond the half page: whether Jordan gets an envelope and restarts Happy, and whether she also gets the 'Happy is down' alert
for the envelope only: T10 passes, run by Tony alone before anything is sealed

for the envelope only: room in a plan. It is built in wave A only if the coded check is not built there and neither the lookup nor Jordan's inbox takes its place; otherwise it is carried to wave B, or waits until a plan has room
caveats: With the half page alone Jordan cannot bring Happy back: after a power cut Happy stays down until Tony unlocks the Mac at home, which is what the roadmap row he chose says.
A small UPS only bridges short cuts. A long outage still ends at the disk-unlock screen.
If Apple locks the Apple Account that Happy uses, nobody at home can fix it quickly, and iMessage is the only channel.
The page has no pause step: the in-house stop phrase is in no wave, and whether Jordan needs a stop of her own waits on Q9.
If the envelope is added it is a credential on paper: the happy user's password alone already opens every person's agent data, because the gateway keeps it under that account.
At most one envelope. An administrator credential on paper for anyone but Tony is a separate decision that has not been taken; if T10 fails, the choice is that decision or waiting for Tony.
edits.safety: Nothing is granted to any agent and no secret is typed into chat or stored in Happy's memory. The half page holds no credential. The control plane stays Tony's alone; an envelope, if he says yes, holds only the happy user's password, never an administrator credential, and is obvious once used because it is sealed.
unverified: What a parent sees on iMessage when a turn fails: read from the docs and the code, not tried (T8).
For the envelope only: whether the happy user is offered at the disk-unlock screen and its password alone brings Happy back. The secure token status was read; the unlock itself was not tried (T10).
